description: Fixed review cameras for the placeholder room. World metres, +Y up, -Z forward (north). Positions do not follow the avatars, so captures stay comparable while the avatar profile changes. The first five are the Run 1 baseline and never change, because the scoring history depends on them; diorama_high and iso_room were added for the founder's 6 October art direction (high-angle and isometric views with a tilt-shift miniature feel). Focus points sit on the player's spawn or on the two avatars, whose reach and figures must stay crisp.

clock.note: Review captures pin the hour and date so time of day and season do not drift between rounds. The preset's own default hour is 16.5; 6 October is autumn in the northern hemisphere.

cameras.label: Player eye
cameras.purpose: What the 10 cm player sees: rug, book and doorstop within reach, the table and far wall beyond. Judges near crispness, far softening and how the floor reads at eye level.

cameras.label: Over the shoulder
cameras.purpose: The default play camera: just behind and above the player's left shoulder, the companion beside it. Judges the avatar against the room, its contact shadow, and the diorama depth of field.

cameras.label: Companion
cameras.purpose: In front of the two avatars, a little above companion height, looking back at them with the south-west corner behind. Judges both characters in one frame, their contact shadows and side light.

cameras.label: Low corner
cameras.purpose: Floor level in the north-east corner looking across the room past the box: long floor perspective, contre-jour light, wall bases and corners.

cameras.label: Ceiling corner
cameras.purpose: High in the south-west corner looking down at the whole room: the tabletop-miniature view. Judges palette, warm key against cool shadow, the tilt-shift band and clutter density.

cameras.label: High-angle diorama
cameras.purpose: Run 1 art direction (6 October): a high-angle tilt-shift view framed on the two avatars from in front and to their left, about 1.1 m away at 45 degrees down with a 35-degree lens. Judges the tabletop-miniature read: the avatars and the rug around them crisp, the floor near the bottom of the frame and the far room at the top melting away, and the twilight palette.

cameras.label: Isometric room
cameras.purpose: Run 1 art direction (6 October): an isometric-style overview from high by the north wall, about 35 degrees down (the isometric angle) with a narrow 30-degree lens, in front of the avatars (they face north) and a little to their right, looking across the room behind them to the south wall. Judges whether the whole room reads as an artistic handmade diorama rather than a photograph, with focus on the avatars and the rest of the room softening.

sweep.note: The -Sweep contact sheet: one camera, rows winter, spring, summer and autumn (mid-season days), columns through the day. 18:00 shows the seasonal swing at the same clock time: night in winter, sunset light in autumn, golden afternoon in summer.
